lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: choosing a contribution

objective: Learners generate at least three candidate family-contribution ideas of varying scope, then choose one based on stated criteria (real need, learner's current skill level, and doable within a reasonable timeframe) before any planning begins.
scenario: Before planning any specific steps, the learner brainstorms at least three possible contributions they could make to their household — things that would genuinely help, not just busywork — and picks one using three criteria: it addresses a real need, it fits their current skill level, and it's doable in a reasonable timeframe.
safetyNotes: This is a brainstorming and decision task; no physical task execution happens in this lesson.

tasks.directions: Before brainstorming, name one thing you've noticed your household could use help with recently.
Generate at least three candidate contribution ideas, then evaluate each against the three criteria (real need, fits your skill level, doable soon).

prompts.text: Each candidate idea is checked against all three criteria, not just picked by preference.
Which candidate did you choose, and which criterion (real need, skill level, or timeframe) mattered most in that decision? Explain why.

remediation: If all three candidates are things the learner already does easily (no real stretch or need), reteach by asking a household member directly what would actually help, then adding that idea to the candidate list.
extension: Interview one household member about what they think the household's biggest current need is, and compare that answer to the learner's own three candidates.
